content: Shq1p is a protein that plays a role in the rRNA processing pathway. It was first identified by Pok Yang in the Chanfreau laboratory at UCLA. When Shq1p is depleted, there is a noticeable reduction in the levels of various H/ACA box snoRNAs. These H/ACA box snoRNAs are essential for the pseudouridylation of pre-rRNA. Additionally, the absence of Shq1p affects certain pre-rRNA intermediates. The synthesis of 8S, 18S, and 25S rRNA is dependent on a single precursor molecule known as 35S pre-rRNA. While many intermediates in the rRNA processing pathway have been identified over the past three decades, there remain several proteins involved in this process whose specific functions are not yet fully understood. Shq1p is one such protein, believed to contribute to the stabilization and/or production of H/ACA box snoRNAs, but its precise role remains uncharacterized. It has been hypothesized that Shq1p, in conjunction with Naf1p, participates in the early stages of H/ACA box snoRNP biogenesis. H/ACA box snoRNAs form complexes with proteins to create snoRNPs. Shq1p is thought to associate with certain snoRNP proteins during their maturation process but shows minimal association with the mature snoRNPs. Although Shq1p is known to be involved in the production of H/ACA box snoRNPs, its exact function within the broader rRNA processing pathway remains unclear.
